## Headline

Logitech International grew revenue to USD 1,218.8m [F:cur.revenue] in Q2 FY2027, up 2.8% [F:cur.revenue_yoy]. That is the weakest year-on-year rate since Q4 FY2025. Gross margin improved to 44.9% [F:cur.gross_margin] and net income rose 5.5% [F:cur.net_income_yoy] to USD 180.0m [F:cur.net_income]. Cash generation was weaker: free cash flow fell to USD 148.8m [F:cur.free_cash_flow] from USD 212.3m [F:ly.free_cash_flow], while buybacks rose to USD 170.8m [F:cur.buybacks].

## Growth and profitability

Revenue growth has slowed. Q2 FY2027 growth of 2.8% [F:q2_fy2027.revenue_yoy] compares with 6.9% [F:q1_fy2027.revenue_yoy] in Q1 FY2027 and 6.3% [F:ly.revenue_yoy] in Q2 FY2026. The last period with weaker growth was Q4 FY2025, when revenue declined 0.1% [F:q4_fy2025.revenue_yoy]. For 6M FY2027, revenue reached USD 2,446.1m [F:ytd.revenue], up 4.8% [F:ytd.revenue_yoy].

Gross margin of 44.9% [F:cur.gross_margin] compares with 43.4% [F:ly.gross_margin] a year earlier, a change of +1.5 pp [F:cur.gross_margin_change_yoy].

Operating expenses grew faster than revenue in some lines:

- Selling and marketing rose to 18.0% [F:cur.selling_pct] of revenue from 16.8% [F:ly.selling_pct].
- R&D rose to 6.8% [F:cur.rnd_pct] from 6.4% [F:ly.rnd_pct].
- General and admin held at 3.5% [F:cur.admin_pct].

As a result, operating margin improved only modestly, to 16.5% [F:cur.operating_margin] from 16.1% [F:ly.operating_margin], a change of +0.3 pp [F:cur.operating_margin_change_yoy]. It was also below the 21.1% [F:q1_fy2027.operating_margin] reported for Q1 FY2027. Net margin was 14.8% [F:cur.net_margin] against 14.4% [F:ly.net_margin].

Net income growth of 5.5% [F:cur.net_income_yoy] is well below the 17.3% [F:ly.net_income_yoy] recorded in Q2 FY2026. For 6M FY2027, net income was USD 415.7m [F:ytd.net_income], up 31.3% [F:ytd.net_income_yoy]. That year-to-date figure includes the flagged Q1 FY2027 quarter. The filings data does not explain the margin or expense movements.

## Working capital and cash

**Cash flow.** Operating cash flow fell to USD 163.6m [F:cur.operating_cash_flow] from USD 228.8m [F:ly.operating_cash_flow], and free cash flow fell to USD 148.8m [F:cur.free_cash_flow]. Buybacks of USD 170.8m [F:cur.buybacks] exceeded free cash flow in the quarter. A year earlier, buybacks were USD 106.6m [F:ly.buybacks], below free cash flow. Even so, cash and cash equivalents stood at USD 1,507.6m [F:cur.cash], compared with USD 1,375.8m [F:ly.cash] a year earlier. Trailing cash conversion was 1.25x [F:cur.cash_conversion_ttm], slightly below 1.29x [F:ly.cash_conversion_ttm].

**Inventory.** Inventory reached USD 556.8m [F:cur.inventory], up 7.6% [F:cur.inventory_yoy]. That is faster than revenue growth, and it reverses the 0.5% [F:ly.inventory_yoy] decline seen a year ago. Days inventory outstanding rose to 75 days [F:cur.dio_days] from 70 days [F:ly.dio_days]. This is the highest level in the series and up from 66 days [F:q1_fy2027.dio_days] last quarter.

**Receivables and payables.** Days sales outstanding were unchanged at 55 days [F:cur.dso_days]. Days payables outstanding lengthened to 87 days [F:cur.dpo_days] from 79 days [F:ly.dpo_days]. Longer payables more than offset the inventory build, so the cash conversion cycle improved slightly to 44 days [F:cur.cash_conversion_cycle_days] from 46 days [F:ly.cash_conversion_cycle_days].

## What to watch next quarter

- **Revenue momentum.** We should confirm whether growth of 2.8% [F:cur.revenue_yoy] marks a trend or a single soft quarter. The data does not show the cause.
- **Inventory.** We need to see whether days inventory outstanding of 75 days [F:cur.dio_days] comes back toward recent levels such as 65 days [F:q4_fy2026.dio_days], or keeps rising.
- **Selling and marketing.** Spending at 18.0% [F:cur.selling_pct] of revenue warrants checking. The reason for the increase is not in the pack.
- **Cash returns.** Buybacks ran above free cash flow this quarter. We should check whether operating cash flow recovers.
- **Payables.** We should check whether the longer payables of 87 days [F:cur.dpo_days] can be sustained.

## Data caveats

- **Q1 FY2027 gross margin.** The 49.5% [F:q1_fy2027.gross_margin] reported is an unusual figure that needs checking. It stands well above other recent quarters, such as 44.5% [F:q4_fy2026.gross_margin] in Q4 FY2026.
- **Q1 FY2027 operating margin.** The 21.1% [F:q1_fy2027.operating_margin] reported is an unusual figure that needs checking. It compares with 14.1% [F:q1_fy2026.operating_margin] in Q1 FY2026. Both flagged figures also feed the 6M FY2027 totals.
- **Derived figures.** Q4 figures and most quarterly cash flows are derived as year to date minus the previous year to date. Working-capital days use quarter-end balances over trailing-twelve-month flows.
